content:
miguel: quick heads-up — last night between 02:00-03:00 UTC we saw a spike in request queueing and a small burst of 503s when a couple of GPU pools hit 96% util. p95 token service latency went from 120ms -> 420ms. suspect our static key token-buckets are letting through bursts that overwhelm headroom for inference pods.

ava: saw the same on grafana, tagging the dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/local/d/ops/fleet-saturation?orgId=1&from=now-3h to show the GPU util and queue depth correlation.

jess: ugh. is this the classic problem where token-bucket bursts plus long tail model latencies pile up? do we have per-region headroom signals feeding admission control?

miguel: not currently. we only have per-key token buckets with global refill and an org-level soft cap. proposal: bind refill_rate to a weighted GPU_headroom metric per-region/pool, and add a short-lived per-org leaky-bucket overlay that enforces sustained throughput.

ops-bot: [alert] 2105120123: gpu-pool-us-east-3 util > 95% (15m avg). auto-shed enabled.

dmitri: short replies: +1 for tying refill to headroom, but be careful with chattiness — if refill drops to near-zero during saturation, we might prod cascade failures for low-priority traffic. suggest a graceful degrade path: route excess to lower-cost model variants or queue with a bounded grace window.

jess: agree. maybe implement a proportional refill with floor: refill = max(min_refill, base_refill * (headroom / target_headroom)). that way keys still get limited burst but not completely starved.

miguel: rough sketch config (for discussion):
```yaml
token_bucket:
  capacity: 2000
  base_refill_per_sec: 50
  min_refill_per_sec: 5
  dynamic_refill:
    source: gpu_headroom_metric
    formula: base_refill_per_sec * clamp(headroom_pct / 0.2, 0.1, 3.0)
org_overlay:
  leaky_rate_per_org: 1000
  grace_window_ms: 350
  fallback_model: small-lm-v1
```

ava: that looks reasonable. can we make the headroom metric window shorter (30s) for faster reaction but also add a smoothing factor to avoid oscillations?

dmitri: yes, add an EWMA on headroom with alpha=0.3. also add hysteresis on refill adjustments so we don't thrash when pools bounce around 90-95%.

jess: operational question — how do we map API keys to pools/regions? currently requests pick nearest pool, but keys have no affinity. we should keep it simple: compute a weighted sum of headroom across candidate pools for a request's region, fall back to global headroom if ambiguous.

miguel: plan: I'll write a prototype in the admission controller to compute dynamic_refill and a short-lived leaky overlay. will add metrics: per-key refill_rate, per-org leaky_drain_rate, and a new gauge "admission.fallback_rate" for traffic we route to fallback models. will create a canary in us-west-2 with 1% traffic.

ava: tagging the SLO owners and docs — @jess please include the metric names and a dashboard panel. @dmitri can you review the EWMA/hysteresis math?

jess: will do. also please include a feature flag + rollout plan in the PR so we can quickly revert if we see increased 5xxs.

dmitri: quick nit — consider also adding a small "emergency credit" pool for enterprise reserved capacity so we don't throttle committed customers during noisy neighbor events. credits should be charged and then slowly refilled.

miguel: good call. I'll add enterprise_credit config and a top-level priority check before the leaky overlay.

ops-bot: [deploy] admission-controller/prototype branch pushed: https://git.redwood/repo/admission-controller/compare/feature/dyn-refill

ava: nice. tagging oncall for the canary window. @oncall please watch gpu-pool-util and admission.fallback_rate for the next 2h after rollout.

jess: quick checklist before we can roll: 1) add EWMA + hysteresis 2) dashboard panels and alerts 3) canary flag 4) enterprise credit test cases. i'll own the dashboard.

miguel: assigned. will send a short RFC tomorrow with config defaults and simulated load tests.

ava: thanks — sounds like a good path forward. :thumbsup:
